query: What is the current level of crude oil in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve as of June 2026, per EIA weekly data (WCSSTUS1)? What has been the weekly trajectory over the past 3-6 months (fills or releases)?
answer:
I've completed the research on US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude oil levels. Here's the summary:

## Key Findings

**Current Level (June 2026):** Per EIA weekly data (WCSSTUS1), SPR crude stood at **325.7 million barrels** for the last June reading (week ending June 26, 2026), falling further to **319.5 million barrels** by July 3 — the **lowest level since 1983** and down ~20.7% year-over-year.

**Weekly Trajectory (3–6 months):** Two distinct phases:
- **Jan–late March:** Flat to slightly rising, plateauing at ~415.4 million barrels (period peak, held unchanged mid-Feb through late March).
- **April–July:** Accelerating **drawdown** with weekly releases peaking at ~8–10 million barrels/week. Roughly **96 million barrels drained in ~14 weeks**.

**Driver:** Not routine sales — this is an emergency release. On **March 11, 2026**, the Trump administration announced a **172-million-barrel SPR release** as part of a coordinated IEA action (~400 million barrels across 32 nations) to offset supply disruption from the U.S.–Israel war on Iran. Deliveries began mid-March with a ~120-day timeline, explaining the April lag before draws appeared in the data. Some volumes were structured as loans to oil companies.

All figures were cross-validated across EIA's own data table, YCharts, TradingEconomics, DOE/energy.gov, CNBC, CNN, and Newsweek. Structured output has been submitted.

key_facts: SPR crude oil stood at 325.7 million barrels (325,655 thousand bbl) for the last June 2026 reading, week ending June 26, 2026, per EIA WCSSTUS1.
SPR fell further to 319.5 million barrels (319,489 thousand bbl) by week ending July 3, 2026 - the latest data point.
This is the lowest SPR level since 1983, surpassing the prior low set in July 2023.
SPR is down ~20.7% year-over-year from ~402.8 million barrels one year earlier.
January-late March 2026: SPR was flat to slightly rising, plateauing at ~415.4 million barrels (the period peak) held unchanged from mid-Feb through late March.
April-July 2026: accelerating drawdown, with weekly releases peaking at roughly 8-10 million barrels/week in May-June.
Total drawdown from the ~415.4 million barrel peak (late March) to 319.5 million barrels (July 3) was about 96 million barrels over ~14 weeks.

Driver: On March 11, 2026, the Trump administration announced a 172-million-barrel SPR release as part of a coordinated IEA action (~400 million barrels across 32 nations) to offset supply disruption from the U.S.-Israel war on Iran.
Deliveries began mid-March and were expected to take ~120 days, explaining the lag before draws appeared in EIA data in April.
Some releases were structured as loans/exchanges; DOE loaned 26.03 million barrels to nine oil companies in an April batch (the third allotment).
